statusDefinitions.UNKNOWN: Required source data or evidence is absent, ambiguous, incomplete, or cannot be refreshed.
statusDefinitions.PARTIAL: Reusable evidence exists, but the complete proof is not accepted.
statusDefinitions.PLANNED: The proof is defined but no accepted evidence exists yet.
statusDefinitions.DOCUMENTARY_ONLY: The concern requires policy, compatibility, or support evidence rather than a short live demonstration.
statusDefinitions.ACCEPTED: Accepted evidence is bound to an exact evidence ID, subject version and digest, platform release, configuration digest, and verification time.
statusDefinitions.STALE: Previously accepted evidence no longer matches the current subject, platform release, configuration, or qualification baseline and is not current proof.

items.concern: Deterministic software lifecycle with explicit download, install, activation, stop, update, and single-active-instance state.
items.acceptanceCriterion: Every requested transition reaches one unambiguous authoritative state or an explicit unresolved state and never exposes two active instances.
items.claimBoundary: Existing lifecycle evidence does not yet prove the complete G0-G4 graph or dashboard presentation; Cloud transition duration is not a first-demo vehicle KPI.

items.concern: Per-service persistent storage with declared ownership, quota, isolation, update survival, and removal policy.
items.acceptanceCriterion: The service retains only declared state across update and restart, cannot read another service store, and follows the accepted removal policy.
items.claimBoundary: No accepted Brake Health service storage contract exists yet.

items.concern: Predictable recovery after ignition-like power loss, restart, and interrupted update without identity or accepted state loss.
items.acceptanceCriterion: After every approved interruption point, the Unit returns to the last accepted state with the same identity and an explicit recovery result.
items.claimBoundary: VM persistence is qualified; application state across all future update phases is not.

items.concern: Bounded platform and service startup/readiness suitable for an automotive boot sequence.
items.acceptanceCriterion: Measured readiness percentiles satisfy an accepted threshold over a declared sample set.
items.claimBoundary: Successful boot is known; accepted timing thresholds and repeated measurements are not complete.

items.concern: Artifact authenticity and integrity verification before activation.
items.acceptanceCriterion: Only the reviewed digest signed by an accepted trust anchor activates; a modified artifact is rejected.
items.claimBoundary: Local provider signing evidence exists; the full staged provider/service Cloud flow is not accepted.

items.concern: AosCore-enforced per-service resource quotas with observed use and isolation between two in-vehicle service tenants.
items.acceptanceCriterion: The actual Tire service reaches but cannot exceed its approved CPU quota under AosCore enforcement, while Brake processes the deterministic event without restart and the platform remains healthy; Tire returns to normal after the load stops.
items.claimBoundary: The first live proof covers CPU isolation between one Aos-managed service instance per Service Provider. Mac-local backends, aggregate multi-service-per-provider quotas, and audience-visible memory, storage, PID, or network saturation are excluded.

items.concern: Efficient fleet delivery, including measured payload and transfer savings for an update.
items.acceptanceCriterion: The dashboard reports measured transferred bytes and savings against the full artifact without assigning an unverified delta-update label.
items.claimBoundary: Differential or chunk-reuse behavior has not been measured in the current environment.

items.concern: Dependency-aware installation and activation across platform FOTA capabilities and SOTA services.
items.acceptanceCriterion: Existing component-to-component and service-to-layer dependencies remain visible as supported platform capabilities. After the cross-lifecycle roadmap capability is released, AosCloud rejects a service whose required FOTA Vehicle Data Platform Component version is absent before Subject-service desired-state change or Unit transfer; service readiness remains fail-closed defense in depth.
items.claimBoundary: The current released Cloud/API supports component-to-component and service-to-layer dependencies but has no documented Service-to-FOTA Vehicle Data Platform Component admission rule. Only that cross-lifecycle rejection is deferred to the AosEdge roadmap release; no project-side admission controller is planned.

items.concern: Defined long-term support, vulnerability response, and maintenance ownership.
items.acceptanceCriterion: A reviewed support record names maintained versions, ownership, support dates, and vulnerability-response expectations.
items.claimBoundary: A short live demo cannot prove a multi-year support commitment.

items.concern: Versioned and backward-compatible APIs between vehicle platform capabilities and post-SOP services.
items.acceptanceCriterion: The old consumer remains compatible through the declared range and an incompatible combination is rejected before activation.
items.claimBoundary: Versioning intent exists, but the staged compatibility matrix is not yet accepted.

items.concern: Trusted, immutable artifact sources without reliance on mutable tags or uncontrolled public registries.
items.acceptanceCriterion: Every promoted artifact resolves to an immutable digest from an approved source with retained provenance.
items.claimBoundary: The dashboard and service OCI provenance contract are not implemented.

items.concern: Visibility of transitive dependencies, software bill of materials, and known vulnerability findings.
items.acceptanceCriterion: Each candidate has a digest-bound SBOM and a time-stamped vulnerability-policy verdict before promotion.
items.claimBoundary: No accepted SBOM and vulnerability evidence pipeline exists for the complete demo graph.

items.concern: Least-privilege device and vehicle-interface access without broad host privilege.
items.acceptanceCriterion: The component performs its declared function with only approved capabilities and interfaces while forbidden access is denied.
items.claimBoundary: The provider boundary has SELinux evidence; the future Brake Health service policy is not accepted.

items.concern: Safe vehicle/cohort targeting with a guard against intended-versus-effective recipient mismatch.
items.acceptanceCriterion: Promotion is visibly blocked or explicitly re-approved when effective recipients differ from the reviewed target set.
items.claimBoundary: A real stale-batch targeting defect is documented; the dashboard guard is not implemented.

items.concern: Continued local function during connectivity loss plus bounded reconnect, queue, and replay behavior.
items.acceptanceCriterion: Local Brake Health processing remains available without Cloud connectivity and buffered output follows the accepted replay policy after recovery.
items.claimBoundary: VM network mobility is improved; Brake Health offline processing and replay are not implemented.

items.concern: Bounded idle CPU, memory, network activity, and battery-impact proxy.
items.acceptanceCriterion: The accepted idle observation window remains below declared CPU, memory, network, and wakeup thresholds.
items.claimBoundary: A Mac/QEMU proxy is not a physical vehicle battery measurement.

items.concern: Detection and safe handling of unhealthy OS, driver, runtime, or dependency state.
items.acceptanceCriterion: A controlled failure is detected at the correct layer, unsafe activation is prevented, and recovery is explicit and bounded.
items.claimBoundary: VM and runtime recovery evidence exists; the full layered fault matrix is incomplete.

items.concern: Coordinated release view spanning base system/FOTA capabilities and SOTA services, with firmware scope stated separately.
items.acceptanceCriterion: The dashboard presents one dependency-aware release graph and clearly labels any firmware outside the demonstrated pipeline.
items.claimBoundary: Rootfs and platform-component work exists; physical ECU and Wi-Fi firmware update are not demonstrated.

items.concern: Per-vehicle identity, certificate lifecycle, secret isolation, and key-rotation readiness.
items.acceptanceCriterion: Each Unit keeps a unique identity, artifacts exclude secrets, expiration is visible, and the accepted rotation path is documented and tested where supported.
items.claimBoundary: Persistent mTLS identity is proven in the VM; hardware TPM behavior and complete rotation are not.

items.concern: Integrated operational workflow that avoids presenting a collection of unrelated tools as one platform capability.
items.acceptanceCriterion: The demonstrator can follow one release and evidence timeline while every external dependency and owner remains explicit.
items.claimBoundary: A unified dashboard is planned; the demo must not claim that all external systems disappear.

items.concern: Measured end-to-end local event latency and serialization/network-hop cost.
items.acceptanceCriterion: The local VISS-to-advisory path meets an accepted latency percentile while Cloud connectivity is absent.
items.claimBoundary: The value is bounded local processing without a Cloud round trip, not elimination of IPC or serialization overhead.
